children: US stocks rose on Wednesday, September 16, as the Federal Reserve decided to raise interest rates for the first time in three years. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) edged up roughly 0.1%, while the S&P 500 (GSPC) rose 0.4%. The Nasdaq Composite (IXIC) gained 0.7%.

Investors will track a batch of key US economic data on Thursday, including August housing starts, the September Philadelphia Fed Business Outlook Survey and weekly jobless claims, all due at 8:30 am ET. August pending home sales data, which measures the month-on-month change, will follow at 10 am ET.
Foreign institutional investors remained net sellers of Indian equities on Wednesday, September 16, offloading shares worth ₹2,032.61 crore, according to provisional data from the exchanges.

At the end of the US Federal Reserve’s two-day policy meeting, the Fed dot plot indicates that the Fed is not done yet. Most policymakers expect at least one more rate increase in the coming months, while a handful see the possibility of two additional hikes.
Oil prices surged as fresh supply threats from Saudi Arabia and Libya compounded losses already stemming from the Iran war.

title: Market Pulse: Key triggers to watch before the September 17 trading session
